text:
marta: onboarding NuQuestra LoRA merge into sandbox. quick signal: embedding recall drop on cust_faqs after our OPTQ int4 pass. opening triage.

lee: uploaded quick-eval: https://internal.redwood/quick-evals/5067894321 — summary embed_recall 0.91 -> 0.76, mean cosine delta -0.15. :frowning:

omar: ran a tiny repro and found tokenizer variance on decimal & currency separators and list bullets. minimized example below.

```
orig: \"Invoice total: 1,234.56 USD • due 2026-04-01\"
tokens(base): [120, 4023, 77, 901, ...]
tokens(nuquestra-adapter): [120, 4023, 44211, 77, 901, ...]  // adapter glued comma+decimal into single token
```

ciara: noted that the merge CI used OPTQ int4 with fold-v2.2. small numeric folding differences can amplify after quant. when I ran no-quant the recall drop was ~0.02; with optq-int4 it's ~0.15. so quant + tokenizer mismatch is the likely culprit.

eval-bot: [auto] quickpack finished: /artifacts/5067894321/quickpack.json — generation metrics pass; embedding_recall FAILED (delta -0.15). reranker_passrate 0.94 -> 0.69.

marta: options on table: 1) merge-time tokenizer shim to normalize comma/decimal/currency/bullets, 2) try bnb int8 deploy for this customer, 3) re-export adapter with prod tokenizer and re-run, 4) tiny 100–200 step anchor-finetune to re-anchor faq vectors.

omar: prototype tokenizer shim idea: a lightweight preprocessor mapping commonly-seen separators to canonical tokens that match adapter training preproc. I'll add unit tests.

lee: repro command for investigators:

```
./run_quick_eval.sh --model nuquestra-lora:merge-v1 --quant optq-int4 --dataset cust_faqs --seed 21 --limit 40
```

(6m)

lee: paste of top 3 human diffs from limit=40 run:
1) Q: "How do I update billing?"
   base top1: "Go to settings > Billing"
   nuquestra top1: "Update billing in account"  // semantically OK but cosine drops 0.06 -> reranker fails cutoff
2) Q: "What's the refund policy?"
   base: "30 days from purchase"
   nuquestra: "Refunds processed within 30 days"  // order/phrasing shift pushes below threshold
3) Q: "Do you accept EUR?"
   base: "Yes, we show EUR pricing"
   nuquestra: "Shows prices in EUR"  // vector drift removes expected anchor

ciara: reranker thresholds are strict for this customer; small drift is high impact. I'll run a quant matrix after tokenizer shim PR: optq-int4 (fold-v2.2), optq-int4 (fold-v2.4), bnb-int8. also test optq-int4 with layernorm fold-v2.4 since folding changes were recently introduced.

omar: opening draft PR for tokenizer shim + token-diff CI test. PR includes sample failing cases and a script to compare token sequences between base and adapter for quickpacks. PR link: https://git/repo/pull/2087

lee: once PR merges i'll re-run quickpack across quants and also try a small 150-step anchor-finetune sim to see recall recovery without full retrain. will record embedding_recall + reranker_passrate deltas.

marta: eval-bot — please update quickpack recipe to include reranker_passrate, token-diff histogram, and top-k human diffs in the artifact.

eval-bot: [auto] noted — quickpack recipe updated per request by @marta. new artifact fields: reranker_passrate, token_diff_histogram, top_human_diffs.

ciara: timeline: get tokenizer shim PR in 24h, run quant matrix and anchor-finetune sim on canary, mitigation decision within 48h. filing INF-521 for CS handoff and tracking. tagging @eng-ml and @customer-success. :thumbsup:

omar: +1. includes a small README in the PR describing why token boundaries amplify post-quant and how the shim works. will add CI that fails merges if token-diff histogram shows >1% boundary changes on quickpack baseline.

marta: thanks — once you post the canary artifacts here we'll decide whether int8 deploy or shim+anchor-finetune is the fastest path to restore customer recall.
